scope.flow: _matchIncomingOrder quote-denominated fill order matching with lot-size flooring

statements.text: The incoming fill order is quote-denominated (amountIsBase = false).
A lot-size constraint is present (e.g., lotSizeInBase = 1e18) so lot-size flooring can reduce the tradeable base amount.
The incoming order has a remaining quote amount (e.g., taker.amount = 2.5e18) and maker base liquidity is available (e.g., maker base = 3e18).
_matchIncomingOrder computes potential_base, matchedBase, baseDelta via lot-size flooring, and quoteDelta for the incoming order.
When baseDelta != matchedBase, the system sets matchedAmount = takerOrder.amount (full remaining quote) instead of quoteDelta.
The incorrect matchedAmount is used to decrement the incoming order's remaining amount in the bid and ask matching loops.
Over-subtraction of the remaining amount causes the matching loop to terminate prematurely, preventing the order from continuing to match against additional liquidity.

For Fill-or-Kill orders, the FOK validation check passes because newOrder.amount was incorrectly reduced to 0 even though dust quote amount remains unfilled, violating the all-or-nothing FOK guarantee.

Users receive fewer base tokens than their quote amount should purchase; settlement uses the correct smaller quoteDelta and baseDelta, but the order is marked fully filled despite only partial execution.
In the example, the order amount is reduced by 2.5 units while only 2 units worth of base tokens are traded, resulting in a 20% loss of expected value.

The incoming order's remaining amount should be decremented by the actual quote amount consumed (quoteDelta), so matching continues against additional liquidity and the order is not marked fully filled while unfilled quote remains.
A Fill-or-Kill order should either execute completely or fail entirely, not pass validation while dust quote amount remains unfilled.

ambiguities: Report does not state who submits the order or any authorization/permission condition; no unauthorized-caller claim is made.
